chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: More labels: Julie London, Dameron's 'John's Delight', Billie Holiday and Teddy Wilson
summary: He cites Vic Dickenson sessions, solos on Julie London dubbing, John's Delight and Focus with J. J. Johnson, and I Hear Music with Teddy Wilson.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yes. Here's the thing that I did with Julie London. I never even played this, but I had solos all

through this because we did this with --we recorded it and then she over dubbed, and so I had to take all these solos and tunes, melodies that I didn't even hear. But any way, okay. As you know I've done so many things with Ella, I just -- with Benny Carter, I just can't -- it's amazing. I don't understand it.
How can they do this to me?
John, maybe we should write a book.

Here's the one I did with Tad Dameron, 'John's Delight.' I wrote this one, you know. Let's see, who's featured on the record. They don't give you the personnel of the band, only who was featured on the record. It's Tad Dameron, piano, J. J. Johnson, trombone, and John Collins, guitar, featured. Okay. On the other side is focus. They only give the featured artist, Cecil Payne, baritone, J. J. Johnson, trombone, John Collins, guitar. How can they do this to me? I won't tell you how many records I made with Slam when I was with his group, I -- here we are again. 'I Hear Music', Billie Holiday, with Teddy Wilson, Roy Eldridge, Al Hall, John Collins, guitar.
Oh, have I convinced you? 'I'm All For You.' Here we are again. Teddy Wilson, John Collins, Al Hall, Jimmy Hamilton, I think this is Don -- no, let's see. George Georgia
Auld Byas Art, and Don Byas. Sure. So you see, this is sickening. I mean, I just -- I -- I just don't understand it. You know.
